source.title: $\textit{Revelio}$: Interpreting and leveraging semantic information in diffusion models
source.authors: Dahye Kim; Xavier Thomas; Deepti Ghadiyaram

record.tranche_reason: The study uses k-sparse autoencoders to interpret diffusion-model features, but does not test the claimed audit of a model's own neuron poles or any listed version.
record.gate_note: The reported k-SAE label-purity and GPT-4o granularity measurements concern learned autoencoder features, not the diffusion models' own neurons. They are recorded as related findings under fits_no_version. Diff-C classification and visual-reasoning scores are downstream task results, not measurements of neuron interpretability. The PCA discussion is qualitative and does not quantify the share of interpretable neurons.
record.test_reason: The study trains k-sparse autoencoders on pooled diffusion-model activations and measures the label purity of the learned SAE features. It never audits the diffusion models' own neurons, language-model neurons, InceptionV1, attribution graphs or simulation scores. It asserts without testing that reading interpretable units directly from layer activations is "not viable", which assumes the opposite of V4 and V1–V2. It neither tests nor relies on the claim, so T6 rather than the reader's T4.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that k-SAEs isolate monosemantic visual features in diffusion models. They find visual abstraction oscillates from coarse to fine and back to coarse with depth, and varies with timestep, architecture (U-Net vs DiT), pre-training data and latent vs pixel space. They also find diffusion features transfer well to classification and visual reasoning via the lightweight Diff-C.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains k-sparse autoencoders on spatially pooled diffusion-model activations and assesses learned-feature purity and visual granularity; it does not audit model-neuron poles or validate written neuron explanations on held-out activations.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported k-SAE label purity varies with diffusion layer, timestep, dataset, model, and DiT block; GPT-4o granularity judgments are described as sensitive to system prompt.

fits_no_version.finding: k-SAE features from SD 1.5 layers differ in class-label purity across layers and datasets: up ft1 is lowest for Oxford-IIIT Pet, bottleneck for Caltech-101 and ImageNet.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Class-label purity of SAE features learned on diffusion activations depends on layer and task granularity.

fits_no_version.finding: SAE-feature label purity varies with timestep (t=25 is best for Pet/up ft1, t=200 for Caltech/bottleneck), with model (SD 1.5 is purer than SD 2.1) and with DiT block (block 14 is lowest).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE-feature purity in diffusion models depends on timestep, model variant and block depth.

fits_no_version.finding: GPT-4o judged only 1–2% of image sets from the top 100 k-SAE neurons as having no detectable pattern, across the four layers. Fine-grained judgments peak at up ft1 (47%). The authors call these judgments noisy and prompt-sensitive.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Nearly all top-activating SAE features in diffusion U-Nets show some recognizable pattern to an LLM judge (about 98–99%).

fits_no_version.finding: DiT SAE-feature label purity is slightly worse at 256 than at 512 resolution in all blocks.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Input resolution modestly changes SAE-feature purity in DiT.

record.peer_reviewed: IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision
record.problems: The study's label-purity measure is a proxy based on class labels among highly activating images, not a direct test of whether a model neuron has one job. The authors note that GPT-4o predictions can be noisy and system-prompt-sensitive. No uncertainty estimates are given for the reported purity values.
record.rows_left_out: Omitted Diff-C transfer-learning and LLaVA visual-reasoning outcomes because they measure downstream task performance rather than the interpretability properties at issue. Omitted qualitative visualization and PCA descriptions because they do not supply a separate numerical result.

untested.parts: No Qwen3-32B neuron-pole audit or shares of one-job, two-job or unknown neurons.
No language models of any architecture or scale; diffusion models only, and only via SAE features.
No InceptionV1 neurons, pose features or recursive-generalization analysis.
No share of interpretable native neurons, and no test of whether tools or architecture raise that share. The U-Net versus DiT comparison concerns SAE-feature label purity only.
No attribution graphs or circuit analysis with native neurons.
No held-out prediction test of explanations.

record.verdict_notes: No verdicts: no row measures native-neuron interpretability. The paper states without evidence that direct interpretation of layer activations is not viable; this is an assumption, not a result bearing on V4. The Table 1 subject/layer mislabel on R25 duplicates up ft1 and drops bottleneck.

versions.untested_parts: No Qwen3-32B audit, neuron-pole job counts, or estimate of the share of poles with one, two, or unknown jobs.
No audit of language models or scaling to dense or mixture-of-experts models or trillion-parameter sizes.
No InceptionV1 cat-and-car example, pose feature, or recursive-generalization versus superposition test.

The paper compares diffusion feature granularity across layers and architectures, but does not estimate the share of interpretable model neurons or test the stated InceptionV1-sized vision-model percentages.
No attribution graphs or test of explaining behavior using the model's own neurons.
No test of explanations against held-out neuron-activating examples or where neurons fire.
No automated simulation score for neuron explanations on new text.
